answer: In an economy where agents trade shale maps, river delta forecasts, and quartz assays, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, with no bonus per identity. Splitting 1,000 locked tokens among a thousand agents gives exactly the same influence as one agent holding them all. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying their purchase price and losing access to that capital during the lock.
